examples.x: There's no love lost between her and her in-laws.

senses.definition_vi: có cảm xúc rất mạnh mẽ của sự yêu thích và quan tâm đối với ai đó

senses.definition: beautiful; attractive

examples.x: She looked particularly lovely that night.
He has a lovely voice.
You've got lovely eyes.
We travelled through some lovely countryside.
She's got an absolutely lovely face.

senses.definition_vi: xinh đẹp; hấp dẫn

senses.definition: very pleasant; wonderful

examples.x: ‘Can I get you anything?’ ‘A cup of tea would be lovely.’
What a lovely surprise!
How lovely to see you!
Isn't it a lovely day?
We've had a lovely time.
It's a lovely old farm.
It's been lovely having you here.
You've got yourself into a lovely mess, haven't you?
to smell/taste/sound lovely

senses.definition_vi: rất dễ chịu; tuyệt vời

senses.definition: very kind, generous and friendly

examples.x: Her mother was a lovely woman.
He is a lovely little boy.
She is a lovely old lady and always full of laughter.

senses.definition_vi: rất tốt bụng, hào phóng và thân thiện

senses.definition: used when you are emphasizing that something is good because of the quality mentioned

examples.x: It's lovely and warm in here.

senses.definition_vi: dùng để nhấn mạnh rằng điều gì đó tốt đẹp vì phẩm chất được đề cập

senses.definition: not high or tall; not far above the ground

examples.x: a low wall/building/table
The fence is too low.
a low range of hills
low clouds
flying at low altitude
The sun was low in the sky.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: at or near the bottom of something

examples.x: low back pain
the lower slopes of the mountain
temperatures in the low 20s (= no higher than 21–23°)

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: not high at the neck

examples.x: a dress with a low neckline

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: below the usual or average amount, level or value

examples.x: a low level of unemployment
lower prices/costs
the lowest rates of interest for 40 years
the lowest temperature ever recorded
low-income families
a low-cost airline
There is a low risk of failure.
Incomes are significantly lower than in other parts of the country.
areas with relatively low unemployment
This yogurt is very low in fat.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: below the usual water level

examples.x: The reservoir was low after the long drought.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: having a reduced amount or not enough of something

examples.x: Our supplies are running low (= we only have a little left).
Our stocks of food were getting low.
A warning light flashes when the battery is low.
They were low on fuel.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: below the usual or expected standard

examples.x: Students with the lowest scores retook the test.
low marks/grades
a low standard of living

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: below other people or things in importance or status

examples.x: lower forms of life (= creatures with a very simple structure)
jobs with low status
Training was given a very low priority.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: not very good

examples.x: She has a very low opinion of her own abilities.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: not high; not loud

examples.x: The cello is lower than the violin.
They were speaking in low voices.
Keep your voice low.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: weak or depressed; with very little energy

examples.x: I'm feeling really low.
They were in low spirits.
I think he got a bit low when he had the flu.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: not honest

examples.x: He mixes with some pretty low types.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: not bright

examples.x: The lights were low and romance was in the air.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: if a vehicle is in low gear, it travels at a slower speed in relation to the speed of the engine
senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: produced with the tongue in the lowest possible position
senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: in a poor state; worse than usual

examples.x: Morale among teachers is at a low ebb.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: to lose your wealth or your high position in society
senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: the amount of attention somebody/something has from the public

examples.x: This issue has had a high profile in recent months.
I advised her to keep a low profile for the next few days (= not to attract attention).
The story was given a low profile in today's papers.

senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: if somebody is laid low by/with an injury or illness, they feel very weak and are unable to do much
senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: people who are not respected at all because they are not honest, moral or important at all
senses.definition_vi: một mức độ hoặc điểm thấp; một con số thấp

senses.definition: to reduce something or to become less in value, quality, etc.

examples.x: He lowered his voice to a whisper.
This drug is used to lower blood pressure.
to lower the rate/cost/price/level of something
Her voice lowered as she spoke.
The company may be forced to lower prices in order to stay competitive.
a proposal to lower the voting age to 16
The company has lowered its expectations for profits this year.
We are not prepared to lower our academic standards.
Mild exercise three times a week significantly lowers your risk of cancer.
The drives were allowed to idle until the temperatures lowered and stabilized.

senses.definition_vi: làm giảm một cái gì đó hoặc trở nên ít hơn về giá trị, chất lượng, v.v.

senses.definition: to let or make something/somebody go down

examples.x: He had to lower his head to get through the door.
She lowered her newspaper and looked around.
They lowered him down the cliff on a rope.
The coffin is lowered into the grave and covered with earth.

senses.definition_vi: cho phép hoặc làm cho cái gì đó/ai đó đi xuống

senses.definition: to set a new, lower standard of quality or performance

examples.x: In the current economic climate we may need to lower the bar on quotas.

senses.definition_vi: đặt ra một tiêu chuẩn chất lượng hoặc hiệu suất mới, thấp hơn

senses.definition: to behave in a way that makes other people respect you less

examples.x: I wouldn't lower myself by working for him.

senses.definition_vi: hành xử theo cách khiến người khác ít tôn trọng bạn hơn

senses.definition: to expect more/less from a situation

examples.x: If they can’t afford such a big house, they’ll just have to lower their sights a little.
After failing to get into university, he lowered his sights and got a job in a shop.

senses.definition_vi: mong đợi nhiều hơn/ít hơn từ một tình huống

senses.definition: to increase/decrease the amount of excitement, emotion, etc. in a situation

examples.x: His angry refusal to agree raised the temperature of the meeting.
The government tried to lower the political temperature by agreeing to some of the demands.

senses.definition_vi: tăng/giảm mức độ hứng thú, cảm xúc, v.v. trong một tình huống

senses.definition: good things that happen to you by chance, not because of your own efforts or abilities

examples.x: With any luck, we'll be home before dark.
With a bit of luck, we'll finish on time.
So far I have had no luck with finding a job.
I'm not having much luck with buses.
I never had much luck (= had a successful relationship) with women.
I could hardly believe my luck when he said yes.
It was a stroke of luck that we found you.
By sheer luck nobody was hurt in the explosion.
The only goal of the match came more by luck than judgement.
We wish her luck in her new career.
She wears a red bracelet to bring her luck.
You're in luck (= lucky)—there's one ticket left.
You're out of luck. She's not here.
What a piece of luck!
Finally my luck ran out and they caught me trying to climb the outer wall.

senses.definition_vi: những điều tốt đẹp xảy ra với bạn một cách ngẫu nhiên, không phải do nỗ lực hoặc khả năng của riêng bạn

senses.definition: chance; the force that causes good or bad things to happen to people

examples.x: to have good/bad luck
I put the loss of the money down to pure bad luck.
We had horrible luck with the weather.
In many cultures the colour blue is believed to bring good luck.
myths based on the idea that owls bring bad luck
She dared not trust to luck that nobody would see her.

senses.definition_vi: sự ngẫu nhiên; lực lượng gây ra những điều tốt hoặc xấu xảy ra với mọi người

senses.definition: used to ask somebody if they have been successful with something

examples.x: ‘Any luck?’ ‘No, they're all too busy to help.’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để hỏi ai đó có thành công với điều gì không

senses.definition: in the way that chance decides what will happen

examples.x: As luck would have it, the train was late.

senses.definition_vi: theo cách mà sự ngẫu nhiên quyết định điều gì sẽ xảy ra

senses.definition: used to express sympathy for somebody

examples.x: Bad luck, Helen—you played very well.
It's hard luck on him that he wasn't chosen.
What rotten luck it had to happen now!

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để bày tỏ sự thông cảm với ai đó

senses.definition: to have no money because of a period of bad luck

examples.x: In the movie they play two jazz musicians who are down on their luck.

senses.definition_vi: không còn tiền vì một giai đoạn không may mắn

senses.definition: used to wish somebody success with something

examples.x: The best of luck with your exams.
Good luck! I hope it goes well.
‘I'm going to try giving up social media for a year.’ ‘Good luck with that (= I don't think you will succeed).’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để chúc ai đó thành công với điều gì

senses.definition: used to encourage somebody who has not been successful at something

examples.x: Never mind— better luck next time.
If you didn't win a prize, better luck next time.

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để khuyến khích ai đó đã không thành công với điều gì

senses.definition: because you believe it will bring you good luck, or because this is a traditional belief

examples.x: Take something blue. It's for luck.
I always carry it with me, just for luck.

senses.definition_vi: vì bạn tin rằng nó sẽ mang lại may mắn cho bạn, hoặc vì đây là một niềm tin truyền thống

senses.definition: for no particular reason

examples.x: I gave the mixture one more stir for luck.

senses.definition_vi: vì không có lý do cụ thể

senses.definition: used to say that you do not mind what somebody does as it does not affect you, but you hope they will be successful

examples.x: It's not something I would care to try myself but if she wants to, good luck to her.

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để nói rằng bạn không quan tâm đến việc ai đó làm gì vì nó không ảnh hưởng đến bạn, nhưng bạn hy vọng họ sẽ thành công

senses.definition: used to tell somebody that you feel sorry for them

examples.x: ‘Failed again, I'm afraid.’ ‘Oh, hard luck.’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để nói rằng bạn cảm thấy tiếc cho ai đó

senses.definition: used to show you are not surprised something bad has happened to you, because you are not often lucky

examples.x: Just my luck to arrive after they had left.
Just my luck to get the broken chair!

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để cho thấy bạn không ngạc nhiên khi điều tồi tệ xảy ra với mình, vì bạn không thường gặp may mắn

senses.definition: used to say that somebody has been lucky or successful

examples.x: On a Sunday I didn’t expect to find him at his desk but my luck was in.

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để nói rằng ai đó đã may mắn hoặc thành công

senses.definition: the fact that chance decides something, in a way that you cannot control

examples.x: To a large extent the life you have depends on who your parents were; it’s just the luck of the biological draw.

senses.definition_vi: sự thật là sự ngẫu nhiên quyết định điều gì đó, theo cách bạn không thể kiểm soát

senses.definition: used to show that you are disappointed because something you were hoping for did not happen

examples.x: ‘Were you chosen for the team?’ ‘No such luck!’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để cho thấy bạn thất vọng vì điều gì đó bạn hy vọng đã không xảy ra

senses.definition: when you take pot luck, you choose something or go somewhere without knowing very much about it, but hope that it will be good, pleasant, etc.

examples.x: It's pot luck whether you get good advice or not.
You're welcome to stay to supper, but you'll have to take pot luck (= eat whatever is available).

senses.definition_vi: khi bạn tùy duyên, bạn chọn một thứ gì đó hoặc đi đến một nơi nào đó mà không biết nhiều về nó, nhưng hy vọng rằng nó sẽ tốt, dễ chịu, v.v.

senses.definition: to take a risk because you have successfully avoided problems in the past

examples.x: You didn't get caught last time, but don't push your luck!

senses.definition_vi: để chấp nhận rủi ro vì bạn đã tránh được các vấn đề trong quá khứ

senses.definition: used to show sympathy for somebody that something bad that has happened to

examples.x: ‘I failed by one point.’ ‘That's tough luck.’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để bày tỏ sự thông cảm với ai đó khi điều tồi tệ đã xảy ra với họ

senses.definition: used to show that you do not feel sorry for somebody who has a problem

examples.x: ‘If you take the car, I won't be able to go out.’ ‘Tough luck!’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để cho thấy bạn không cảm thấy tiếc cho ai đó đang gặp vấn đề

senses.definition: to do something that involves risk or luck, hoping to succeed

examples.x: My grandparents emigrated to Canada to try their luck there.

senses.definition_vi: để làm điều gì đó liên quan đến rủi ro hoặc may mắn, hy vọng thành công

senses.definition: used to show that you are disappointed about something

examples.x: I shall have to miss the party, worse luck!

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để cho thấy bạn thất vọng về điều gì đó

senses.definition: having good luck

examples.x: His friend was killed and he knows he is lucky to be alive.
She was lucky enough to be chosen for the team.
You were lucky (that) you spotted the danger in time.
In terms of my career I feel incredibly lucky.
You can think yourself lucky you didn't get mugged.
She counted herself lucky that she still had a job.
Mark is one of the lucky ones—he at least has somewhere to sleep.
the lucky winners
He was among the lucky ones who escaped with only minor injuries.

senses.definition_vi: có may mắn

senses.definition: being the result of good luck

examples.x: It was lucky for us that we were able to go.
Lucky for her, a police car was passing.
It is lucky (that) neither was killed in the accident.
That was the luckiest escape of my life.
a lucky guess
A lucky find on the edge of the Cotswolds is helping archaeologists discover what life was like in Roman Britain.
I had a lucky break when I left school getting a job on local radio.

senses.definition_vi: là kết quả của may mắn

senses.definition: bringing good luck

examples.x: a lucky charm
The team thinks of me as their lucky mascot.

senses.definition_vi: mang lại may mắn

senses.definition: to have good luck

examples.x: She hopes that some day she'll get lucky and win the jackpot.

senses.definition_vi: có may mắn

senses.definition: to meet somebody new and have sex with them

examples.x: Mike's hoping to get lucky tonight.

senses.definition_vi: gặp ai đó mới và quan hệ tình dục với họ

senses.definition: used to show that you think somebody is lucky to have something, be able to do something, etc.

examples.x: ‘I'm off to Paris.’ ‘Lucky you!’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để cho thấy bạn nghĩ ai đó thật may mắn khi có thứ gì đó, có thể làm gì đó, v.v.

senses.definition: to have good luck

examples.x: We certainly struck it lucky with the weather.

senses.definition_vi: có may mắn

senses.definition: to feel very grateful and lucky about something

examples.x: Just thank your lucky stars you weren’t in the house at the time.

senses.definition_vi: cảm thấy rất biết ơn và may mắn về điều gì đó

senses.definition: used when you have failed to do something twice and hope that you will succeed the third time
senses.definition_vi: được dùng khi bạn đã thất bại trong việc làm điều gì đó hai lần và hy vọng rằng bạn sẽ thành công lần thứ ba

senses.definition: used to tell somebody that something that they are expecting probably will not happen

examples.x: ‘I was hoping to get a ticket for Saturday.’ ‘You'll be lucky.’

senses.definition_vi: được dùng để nói với ai đó rằng điều họ đang mong đợi có lẽ sẽ không xảy ra

senses.definition: used to tell somebody that they will probably not get what they are hoping for, and may not deserve it
senses.definition_vi: được dùng để nói với ai đó rằng họ có lẽ sẽ không nhận được thứ họ đang hy vọng, và có thể không xứng đáng với nó

senses.definition: extremely attractive and impressive; deserving praise

examples.x: The Taj Mahal is a magnificent building.
She looked magnificent in her wedding dress.
You've all done a magnificent job.

senses.definition_vi: cực kỳ hấp dẫn và ấn tượng; xứng đáng được khen ngợi

senses.definition: the official system used for sending and delivering letters, packages, etc.

examples.x: a mail service/train/van
the Royal Mail
regular/postal mail (= rather than email)
Hard copies of the documents are in the mail to you.
We do our business by mail.
Never send cash through the mail.
We did not get any message via mail or email.

senses.definition_vi: gửi một cái gì đó cho ai đó bằng hệ thống bưu chính

senses.definition: letters, packages, etc. that are sent and delivered

examples.x: There isn't much mail today.
I sat down to open the mail.
to send/receive/deliver mail
Is there a letter from them in the mail?
Remember to cancel mail delivery when you go on vacation.

senses.definition_vi: gửi một cái gì đó cho ai đó bằng hệ thống bưu chính

senses.definition: messages/a message sent or received on a computer

examples.x: Check regularly for new mail.
She checked her mail before leaving the hotel.
You've got mail.
incoming/outgoing mail
The company's mail server was down.
You can delete your mails with a single swipe.

senses.definition_vi: gửi một cái gì đó cho ai đó bằng hệ thống bưu chính

senses.definition: used in the title of some newspapers

examples.x: the Mail on Sunday

senses.definition_vi: gửi một cái gì đó cho ai đó bằng hệ thống bưu chính

senses.definition: armour (= clothing to protect the body when fighting) made of small metal rings linked together

examples.x: a coat of mail

senses.definition_vi: gửi một cái gì đó cho ai đó bằng hệ thống bưu chính

senses.definition: being the largest or most important of its kind

examples.x: We have our main meal at lunchtime.
Reception is in the main building.
Poor housing and unemployment are the main problems.
Loss of habitat is the main reason for the bird's decline.
The main thing is to stay calm.

senses.definition_vi: là lớn nhất hoặc quan trọng nhất thuộc loại đó

senses.definition: with the hope of using a particular situation in order to gain some advantage for yourself
senses.definition_vi: với hy vọng sử dụng một tình huống cụ thể để đạt được lợi thế cho bản thân

senses.definition: more than anything else; also used to talk about the most important reason for something

examples.x: They eat mainly fruit and nuts.
‘Where do you export to?’ ‘France, mainly.’
The population almost doubles in summer, mainly because of the jazz festival.
The rise in inflation is mainly due to higher food prices.
People come to libraries mainly to borrow books.
During the day it’ll become mainly dry with clear skies.

senses.definition_vi: hơn bất cứ điều gì khác; cũng được sử dụng để nói về lý do quan trọng nhất cho một cái gì đó

senses.definition: in most cases; used to talk about the largest part of a group of people or things

examples.x: Anorexia is an illness that occurs mainly in adolescents.
The people in the hotel were mainly foreign tourists.

senses.definition_vi: trong hầu hết các trường hợp; được sử dụng để nói về phần lớn nhất của một nhóm người hoặc sự vật

senses.definition: very large or important

examples.x: a major road
Some major international companies refused to do business with them.
He played a major role in setting up the system.
major sporting events
a major issue/factor/project/challenge
We have encountered major problems.
Four major cities agreed to ban diesel cars by 2025.
There were calls for major changes to the welfare system.

senses.definition_vi: một sĩ quan có cấp bậc khá cao trong quân đội hoặc không quân Hoa Kỳ

senses.definition: serious

examples.x: Never mind—it's not major.

senses.definition_vi: một sĩ quan có cấp bậc khá cao trong quân đội hoặc không quân Hoa Kỳ

senses.definition: based on a scale (= a series of eight notes) in which the third note is two whole tones / steps higher than the first note

examples.x: the key of D major
the eight notes of the major scale

senses.definition_vi: một sĩ quan có cấp bậc khá cao trong quân đội hoặc không quân Hoa Kỳ

senses.definition: related to somebody’s main subject of study in college
senses.definition_vi: một sĩ quan có cấp bậc khá cao trong quân đội hoặc không quân Hoa Kỳ

senses.definition: the name or type of a machine, piece of equipment, etc. that is made by a particular company

examples.x: What make of car does he drive?
a Swiss make of watch
There are so many different makes to choose from.
We need to know the make, model and year of your car.

senses.definition_vi: tạo ra hoặc chuẩn bị một cái gì đó bằng cách kết hợp các vật liệu hoặc lắp ráp các bộ phận

senses.definition: trying to get money or an advantage for yourself
senses.definition_vi: tạo ra hoặc chuẩn bị một cái gì đó bằng cách kết hợp các vật liệu hoặc lắp ráp các bộ phận

senses.definition: the act or process of making or producing something

examples.x: strategic decision-making
film-making
dressmaking
tea- and coffee-making facilities
the making of social policy

senses.definition_vi: hành động hoặc quá trình chế tạo hoặc sản xuất một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to make somebody become a better or more successful person

examples.x: University was the making of Joe.

senses.definition_vi: làm cho ai đó trở thành một người tốt hơn hoặc thành công hơn

senses.definition: to have the qualities that are necessary to become something

examples.x: Her first novel has all the makings of a classic.
He has the makings of a first-rate lawyer.

senses.definition_vi: có những phẩm chất cần thiết để trở thành một cái gì đó

senses.definition: in the process of becoming something or of being made

examples.x: This model was two years in the making.
These events are history in the making.

senses.definition_vi: trong quá trình trở thành một cái gì đó hoặc đang được tạo ra

senses.definition: created by you rather than by somebody/something else
senses.definition_vi: được tạo ra bởi bạn thay vì bởi người khác/cái gì đó khác

senses.definition: to show something clearly, especially a feeling, an attitude or a quality

examples.x: Social tensions were manifested in the recent political crisis.

senses.definition_vi: để thể hiện rõ ràng một cái gì đó, đặc biệt là một cảm giác, một thái độ hoặc một phẩm chất

senses.definition: to appear or become easy to notice

examples.x: The symptoms of the disease manifested themselves ten days later.

senses.definition_vi: xuất hiện hoặc trở nên dễ nhận thấy

senses.definition: the 3rd month of the year, between February and April

examples.x: She was born in March.
The meeting is on the fifth of March/March the fifth.
The meeting is on March fifth.
We went to Japan last March.
I arrived at the end of March.
Whale-watching trips begin in early March.
The seeds germinate from March to May.
The study appears in the March issue of the Journal of Paediatrics.

senses.definition_vi: đi bộ với những bước chân cứng nhắc, đều đặn như một người lính

senses.definition: with crazy ideas or behaviour; very silly

examples.x: He's as mad as a March hare but he does a great job.

senses.definition_vi: đi bộ với những bước chân cứng nhắc, đều đặn như một người lính

senses.definition: very large, heavy and solid

examples.x: a massive rock
the massive walls of the castle

senses.definition_vi: rất lớn, nặng và rắn chắc

senses.definition: extremely large or serious

examples.x: The government put massive amounts of money into the health service.
The Chancellor is to announce a massive increase in spending.
These farmers grow crops on a massive scale.
He suffered a massive heart attack.
Their house is massive.
They have a massive great house.
Their appeal is massive in Australia.
The explosion made a massive hole in the ground.
The band's new album was a massive hit.

senses.definition_vi: cực kỳ lớn hoặc nghiêm trọng

senses.definition: very successful or important

examples.x: This band is going to be massive.
There has never been anything like this done here before. It's going to be massive.

senses.definition_vi: rất thành công hoặc quan trọng

senses.definition: having the same colour, pattern, style, etc. and therefore looking attractive together

examples.x: The two sisters wore matching outfits.
a blue silk dress with a matching blue hat
a pine table with four matching chairs

senses.definition_vi: có cùng màu sắc, hoa văn, kiểu dáng, v.v. và do đó trông đẹp mắt với nhau.

senses.definition: equal in number or amount; having the same qualities, etc.

examples.x: The college will provide matching funds (= equal to the amount already raised) to complete the project.
Stem cells from a matching donor were injected into the patient.

senses.definition_vi: bằng về số lượng hoặc số lượng; có cùng phẩm chất, v.v.

senses.definition: used (to ask) if somebody is upset, unhappy, etc. or if there is a problem

examples.x: What's the matter? Is there something wrong?
Is anything the matter?
Is something the matter with Bob? He seems very down.
There's something the matter with my eyes.
‘We've bought a new TV.’ ‘What was the matter with the old one?’
What's the matter with you today (= why are you behaving like this)?
What on earth was the matter with her, she wondered. She’d come here to enjoy herself and here she was, stuck on her own in the hotel.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a subject or situation that you must consider or deal with

examples.x: It's a private matter.
They had important matters to discuss.
She may need your help with some business matters.
financial/legal/political matters
They've agreed in theory, but now we need to discuss practical matters.
The matter should be referred to a senior manager.
Do I have any choice in the matter?
I always consulted him on matters of policy.
It's a matter for the police (= for them to deal with).
It was a matter of some concern to most of those present (= something they were worried about).
It should have been a simple matter to check.
It was no easy matter getting him to change his mind.
Let's get on with the matter in hand (= what we need to deal with now).
I wasn't prepared to let the matter drop (= stop discussing it).
We have sent these concerns to Professor Tribe, and now consider the matter closed (= it is finished).
I did not feel that we had got to the heart of the matter (= the most important part).
And that is the crux of the matter (= the most important thing about the situation).
And then there's the little matter of the fifty pounds you owe me.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: the present situation, or the situation that you are talking about

examples.x: Unfortunately, there is nothing we can do to improve matters.
I'd forgotten the keys, which didn't help matters.
And then, to make matters worse, his parents turned up.
I decided to take matters into my own hands (= deal with the situation myself).
Matters came to a head (= the situation became very difficult) with his resignation.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a situation that involves something or depends on something

examples.x: Learning to drive is all a matter of coordination.
Some people prefer the older version to the new one. It's a matter of taste.
She resigned over a matter of principle.
The government must deal with this as a matter of urgency.
Just as a matter of interest (= because it is interesting, not because it is important), how much did you pay for it?
‘I think this is the best so far.’ ‘Well, that's a matter of opinion (= other people may think differently).’
It's not pure fantasy ! It's a plain matter of fact.
Getting the effect you want is a matter of trial and error.
That's not a problem. It's simply a matter of letting people know in time.
Planning a project is just a matter of working out the right order to do things in.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: physical substance that everything in the world is made of; not mind or spirit

examples.x: to study the properties of matter
This swirling mass of energy and matter is classed as a spiral galaxy.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a substance or things of a particular sort

examples.x: Add plenty of organic matter to improve the soil.
elimination of waste matter from the body
She didn't approve of their choice of reading matter.
There were small lumps of matter floating on the surface.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to add a comment on something that you have just said, usually adding something that you think the other person will be interested in

examples.x: It's a nice place. We've stayed there ourselves, as a matter of fact.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to disagree with something that somebody has just said

examples.x: ‘I suppose you'll be leaving soon, then?’ ‘No, as a matter of fact I'll be staying for another two years.’

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: to be very different

examples.x: I know which area they live in, but whether I can find their house is a different matter.
That's a whole different matter.
I don't mind lizards, but snakes are a different matter.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: to be something serious that you should not joke about
senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to emphasize a statement, especially one that is the opposite of what has just been mentioned

examples.x: A new car would be wonderful but the fact of the matter is that we can't afford one.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to add a comment on something that you have just said

examples.x: I didn't like it much. Nor did the kids, for that matter.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to say that something will definitely happen, although you are not sure when

examples.x: It's only a matter of time before they bring out their own version of the software.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: (as) the usual and correct thing to do

examples.x: We always check people's addresses as a matter of course.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: only a few hours, minutes, etc.

examples.x: It was all over in a matter of minutes.
The bullet missed her by a matter of inches.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to describe a situation that is very important or serious

examples.x: You mustn't let anyone know— it's a matter of life and death.
These talks are a matter of life or death for the factory.
Delivering on time is a matter of life and death for a small company.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: something that has been recorded as being true
senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to say that something is not important

examples.x: If that doesn't work out, no matter, I'll rent for another year or two.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to say that something is always true, whatever the situation is, or that somebody should certainly do something

examples.x: They don't last long no matter how careful you are.
Call me when you get there, no matter what the time is.

senses.definition_vi: quan trọng hoặc có ảnh hưởng quan trọng đến ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: the fifth month of the year, between April and June

examples.x: She was born in May.
The meeting is on the fifth of May/May the fifth.
The meeting is on May fifth.
We went to Japan last May.
I arrived at the end of May.
last May's election
Read about Paris markets in the May issue of the magazine.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để nói rằng điều gì đó có thể xảy ra

senses.definition: to have something as a meaning in the same or another language

examples.x: What does this sentence mean?
What does ‘lark’ mean?
The word ‘Kuching’ means ‘cat’ in Malay.
Many languages use a single word to mean both music and dance.
What is meant by ‘batch processing’?

senses.definition_vi: có nghĩa là gì đó trong cùng một ngôn ngữ hoặc một ngôn ngữ khác

senses.definition: to have something as a meaning; to represent something

examples.x: What do we mean by democracy?
Does the name ‘Jos Vos’ mean anything to you (= do you know who he is)?
The flashing light means (that) you must stop.
The Olympics have come to mean a wide variety of things.

senses.definition_vi: có nghĩa là gì đó; đại diện cho một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to intend to say something on a particular occasion

examples.x: What did he mean by that remark?
‘Perhaps we should try another approach.’ ‘What do you mean? (= I don't understand what you are suggesting.)’
‘What's that supposed to mean?’ demanded John.
What do you mean, you thought I wouldn't mind? (= of course I mind and I am very angry)
What she means is that there's no point in waiting here.
I always found him a little strange, if you know what I mean (= if you understand what I mean by ‘strange’).
I know what you mean (= I understand and feel sympathy). I hated learning to drive too.
It was like—weird. Know what I mean?
I see what you mean (= I understand although I may not agree), but I still think it's worth trying.
See what I mean (= I was right and this proves it, doesn't it)? She never agrees to anything I suggest.
‘But Pete doesn't know we're here!’ ‘That's what I mean! (= that's what I have been trying to tell you.)’
Do you mean Ann Smith or Mary Smith?
Did he mean (that) he was dissatisfied with our service?
You mean (= are you telling me) we have to start all over again?

senses.definition_vi: có ý muốn nói điều gì đó trong một dịp cụ thể

senses.definition: to have something as a purpose or intention

examples.x: What did she mean by leaving so early (= why did she do it)?
Don't laugh! I mean it (= I am serious).
He means trouble (= to cause trouble).
Don't be upset—I'm sure she meant it as a compliment.
He means what he says (= is not joking, exaggerating, etc.).
The chair was clearly meant for a child.
Don't be angry. I'm sure she meant it for the best (= intended to be helpful).
She means to succeed.
I'm sorry I hurt you. I didn't mean to.
I'm feeling very guilty—I've been meaning to call my parents for days, but still haven't got around to it.
I didn't mean you to read the letter.
You're meant to (= you are supposed to) pay before you go in.
I never meant (that) you should come alone.

senses.definition_vi: có một cái gì đó như là mục đích hoặc ý định

senses.definition: to have something as a result or a likely result

examples.x: Spending too much now will mean a shortage of cash next year.
Being frugal doesn't necessarily mean doing without.
Lower energy consumption means less pollution.
Touching the wires means instant death.
Do you have any idea what it means to be poor?
We’ll have to be careful with money but that doesn’t mean (that) we can’t enjoy ourselves.
This new order will mean working overtime.
The injury could mean him missing next week's game.
High unemployment means people are spending less.

senses.definition_vi: có một cái gì đó như là kết quả hoặc một kết quả có khả năng xảy ra

senses.definition: to be of value or importance to somebody

examples.x: Your friendship means a great deal to me.
$20 means a lot (= represents a lot of money) when you live on $100 a week.
Money means nothing to him.
Her children mean the world to her.

senses.definition_vi: có giá trị hoặc tầm quan trọng đối với ai đó

senses.definition: to intend somebody to be or do something

examples.x: I was never meant for the army (= did not have the qualities needed to become a soldier).
Duncan and Makiko were meant for each other (= are very suitable as partners).
His father meant him to be an engineer.
She did everything to get the two of them together, but I guess it just wasn't meant to be.

senses.definition_vi: có ý định ai đó là hoặc làm điều gì đó

senses.definition: to be generally considered to be something

examples.x: This restaurant is meant to be excellent.

senses.definition_vi: thường được coi là một cái gì đó

senses.definition: used to explain or correct what you have just said

examples.x: It was so boring—I mean, nothing happened for the first hour!
She's English—Scottish, I mean.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để giải thích hoặc sửa lại những gì bạn vừa nói

senses.definition: to be serious in your intentions

examples.x: He has the look of a man who means business.
He says he's going to make changes, and I think he means business.

senses.definition_vi: nghiêm túc trong ý định của bạn

senses.definition: to not have any intention of hurting somebody
senses.short_meaning_vi: không cố ý làm tổn thương
senses.definition_vi: không có ý định làm tổn thương ai đó

senses.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying or to ask somebody if they really mean what they say

examples.x: I mean to say, you should have known how he would react!
Do you mean to say you've lost it?

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để nhấn mạnh những gì bạn đang nói hoặc để hỏi ai đó xem họ có thực sự có ý đó không

senses.definition: to have good intentions, although their effect may not be good
senses.definition_vi: có ý định tốt, mặc dù kết quả có thể không tốt

senses.definition: serious and important

examples.x: a meaningful relationship/discussion/experience

senses.definition_vi: nghiêm túc và quan trọng

senses.definition: having a meaning that is easy to understand

examples.x: These statistics are not very meaningful.

senses.definition_vi: có một ý nghĩa dễ hiểu

senses.definition: intended to communicate or express something to somebody, without any words being spoken

examples.x: She gave me a meaningful look.

senses.definition_vi: có ý định truyền đạt hoặc thể hiện điều gì đó cho ai đó, mà không cần lời nói

senses.definition: an action, an object or a system by which a result is achieved; a way of achieving or doing something

examples.x: Email is a highly effective means of communication.
The state is in control of the means of production.
We needed to get to London but we had no means of transport.
Have you any means of identification?
Is there any means of contacting him?
Interest rates are used as a means of controlling borrowing.
They are using peaceful means to achieve their aims.
Music is the best means we have to reach a wide audience.
Equality is an end in itself, not just a means to a goal.
This weed can be controlled by various means.

senses.definition_vi: một hành động, một đối tượng hoặc một hệ thống mà qua đó một kết quả đạt được; một cách để đạt được hoặc làm điều gì đó

senses.definition: the money that a person has

examples.x: a man of means (= a rich man)
People should pay according to their means.
Are the monthly repayments within your means (= can you afford them)?
Try to live within your means (= not spend more money than you have).
Private school fees are beyond the means of most people (= more than they can afford).
He doesn't have the means to hire a lawyer.
She must have independent means (= money that she did not earn) to live in such style.

senses.definition_vi: tiền mà một người có

senses.definition: used to say that you are very willing for somebody to have something or do something

examples.x: ‘Do you mind if I have a look?’ ‘By all means.’

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để nói rằng bạn rất sẵn lòng cho ai đó có hoặc làm điều gì đó

senses.definition: using dishonest methods if honest ones do not work

examples.x: She’s determined to win, by fair means or foul.

senses.definition_vi: sử dụng các phương pháp không trung thực nếu các phương pháp trung thực không hiệu quả

senses.definition: with the help of something

examples.x: The load was lifted by means of a crane.

senses.definition_vi: với sự giúp đỡ của cái gì đó

senses.definition: not at all

examples.x: She is by no means an inexperienced teacher.
We haven't won yet, not by any means.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn toàn không

senses.definition: bad or unfair methods of doing something are acceptable if the result of that action is good or positive

examples.x: He defended a morality in which the end justifies the means.
That's only OK if you believe that the end justifies the means.

senses.definition_vi: các phương pháp xấu hoặc không công bằng để làm điều gì đó được chấp nhận nếu kết quả của hành động đó tốt hoặc tích cực

senses.definition: a thing or an action that is not interesting or important in itself but is a way of achieving something else

examples.x: He doesn't particularly like the work but he sees it as a means to an end.
I don't enjoy studying computing—it's just a means to an end.

senses.definition_vi: một thứ hoặc một hành động không thú vị hoặc quan trọng tự thân nó nhưng là một cách để đạt được điều gì đó khác

senses.definition: the methods and materials available for doing something

examples.x: ways and means of raising money
Newspapers have ways and means of getting hold of secret information.

senses.definition_vi: các phương pháp và tài liệu có sẵn để làm điều gì đó

senses.definition: for a short period of time but not permanently

examples.x: I'm changing my email address but for the meantime you can use the old one.

senses.definition_vi: trong một khoảng thời gian ngắn nhưng không vĩnh viễn

senses.definition: in the period of time between two times or two events

examples.x: My first novel was rejected by six publishers. In the meantime I had written a play.
The next programme starts in five minutes; in the meantime, here’s some music.

senses.definition_vi: trong khoảng thời gian giữa hai thời điểm hoặc hai sự kiện

senses.definition: while something else is happening

examples.x: Leave the cake to cool completely. Meanwhile, make the topping.
The storm is expected to move north today. Concerns are mounting meanwhile for a missing surfer.

senses.definition_vi: trong khi một điều gì đó khác đang xảy ra

senses.definition: in the period of time between two times or two events

examples.x: The doctor will see you again next week. Meanwhile, you must rest as much as possible.
I will put an information pack together and send it to you. Meanwhile, here are some links to useful websites.

senses.definition_vi: trong khoảng thời gian giữa hai thời điểm hoặc hai sự kiện

senses.definition: used to compare two aspects of a situation

examples.x: Stress can be extremely damaging to your health. Exercise, meanwhile, can reduce its effects.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng để so sánh hai khía cạnh của một tình huống

senses.definition: in the middle between a larger and smaller size, amount, length, temperature, etc.

examples.x: There are three sizes—small, medium and large.
a man of medium height/build
a medium steak (= one cooked quite well but not too much)
Cook over a medium heat for 15 minutes.
a medium dry white wine
Choose medium to large tomatoes.

senses.definition_vi: một cách để truyền đạt thông tin, v.v. cho mọi người

senses.definition: used to describe what will happen a long, short, etc. time in the future

examples.x: Such a development seems unlikely, at least in the short term (= it will not happen for quite a long time).
In the longer term, children of depressed mothers are more likely to suffer from childhood depression.
In the long term, our efforts will pay off.

senses.definition_vi: một cách để truyền đạt thông tin, v.v. cho mọi người

senses.definition: worth remembering or easy to remember, especially because of being special or unusual

examples.x: The holiday provided many memorable moments.
a truly memorable occasion/event
Her novels are full of memorable characters.
Olivier gives a memorable performance as Hamlet.
memorable lines/lyrics/phrases
The city is memorable for its fantastic beaches.

senses.definition_vi: xứng đáng để ghi nhớ hoặc dễ dàng để ghi nhớ, đặc biệt là vì nó đặc biệt hoặc khác thường

senses.definition: used when you want to emphasize how small, unimportant, etc. somebody/something is

examples.x: It took her a mere 20 minutes to win.
A mere 2 per cent of their budget has been spent on publicity.
He seemed so young, a mere boy.
You've got the job. The interview will be a mere formality.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng khi bạn muốn nhấn mạnh một người/vật nhỏ bé, không quan trọng, v.v.

senses.definition: used when you are saying that the fact that a particular thing is present in a situation is enough to have an influence on that situation

examples.x: His mere presence (= just the fact that he was there) made her feel afraid.
The mere fact that they were prepared to talk was encouraging.
The mere thought of eating made him feel sick.
The merest (= the slightest) hint of smoke is enough to make her feel ill.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng khi bạn nói rằng sự hiện diện của một điều gì đó trong một tình huống là đủ để ảnh hưởng đến tình huống đó

senses.definition: used meaning ‘only’ or ‘simply’ to emphasize a fact or something that you are saying

examples.x: It is not merely a job, but a way of life.
He said nothing, merely smiled and watched her.
They agreed to go merely because they were getting paid for it.
I'm merely stating what everybody knows anyway.

senses.definition_vi: được sử dụng với nghĩa 'chỉ' hoặc 'đơn giản là' để nhấn mạnh một sự thật hoặc một điều gì đó bạn đang nói

senses.definition: a dirty or untidy state

examples.x: The room was in a mess.
The kids made a mess in the bathroom.
‘What a mess!’ she said, surveying the scene after the party.
My hair's a real mess!

senses.definition_vi: một trạng thái bẩn hoặc lộn xộn

senses.definition: a situation that is full of problems, usually because of a lack of organization or because of mistakes that somebody has made

examples.x: The economy is in a mess.
a financial mess
I feel I've made a mess of things.
How did this whole mess start?
Let's try to sort out the mess.
How do we get out of this mess?
The biggest question is how they got into this mess in the first place.
That’s another fine mess you’ve got us into.
The entire event is a sorry mess.

senses.definition_vi: một tình huống đầy rẫy vấn đề, thường là do thiếu tổ chức hoặc do những sai lầm mà ai đó đã mắc phải

senses.definition: a person who is dirty or whose clothes and hair are not tidy

examples.x: You're a mess!

senses.definition_vi: một người bẩn hoặc có quần áo và tóc không gọn gàng

senses.definition: a person who has serious problems and is in a bad mental condition

examples.x: When my wife left me I was a total mess.

senses.definition_vi: một người gặp vấn đề nghiêm trọng và đang trong tình trạng tinh thần tồi tệ

senses.definition: the excrement (= solid waste matter) of an animal, usually a dog or cat
senses.definition_vi: chất thải (= chất thải rắn) của động vật, thường là chó hoặc mèo

senses.definition: a lot of something

examples.x: There's a mess of fish down there, so get your lines in the water.

senses.definition_vi: rất nhiều thứ

senses.definition: a building or room in which members of the armed forces have their meals

examples.x: the officers’ mess

senses.definition_vi: một tòa nhà hoặc căn phòng nơi các thành viên của lực lượng vũ trang dùng bữa

senses.definition: in a position in the middle of an object, group of objects, people, etc.; between the beginning and the end of something

examples.x: Pens are kept in the middle drawer.
She's the middle child of three.
He was very successful in his middle forties.
a middle-sized room
the middle-income groups in society
The film's middle section was rather dull.

senses.definition_vi: phần của một vật ở khoảng cách bằng nhau với tất cả các cạnh hoặc mặt của nó; một điểm hoặc một khoảng thời gian giữa sự bắt đầu và kết thúc của một cái gì đó

senses.definition: (to take/find) an acceptable course of action that avoids two extreme positions
senses.definition_vi: phần của một vật ở khoảng cách bằng nhau với tất cả các cạnh hoặc mặt của nó; một điểm hoặc một khoảng thời gian giữa sự bắt đầu và kết thúc của một cái gì đó

senses.definition: 12 o’clock at night

examples.x: She heard the clock strike midnight.
They had to leave at midnight.
At/on the stroke of midnight fireworks lit up the sky.
We have to catch the midnight train.
Let’s have a midnight feast tonight (= a secret meal that children like to have in the middle of the night).
They whiled away the midnight hours playing cards.

senses.definition_vi: 12 giờ đêm

senses.definition: a very dark blue colour
senses.definition_vi: một màu xanh đậm

senses.definition: to study or work until late at night
senses.definition_vi: học hoặc làm việc cho đến khuya

senses.definition: to leave a place suddenly and secretly, especially at night, usually in order to avoid paying money that you owe to somebody
senses.definition_vi: rời khỏi một nơi đột ngột và bí mật, đặc biệt là vào ban đêm, thường để tránh trả tiền nợ ai đó

senses.definition: the middle part of something

examples.x: Such beauty was unexpected in the midst of the city.
The house is set in the midst of large gardens.
She appeared from the midst of the crowd.

senses.definition_vi: phần giữa của một cái gì đó

senses.definition: among or with them/us/it/you

examples.x: There is a traitor in our midst.

senses.definition_vi: ở giữa hoặc cùng với họ/chúng ta/nó/bạn

senses.definition: while something is happening or being done; while you are doing something

examples.x: a country in the midst of a recession
She discovered it in the midst of sorting out her father's things.
She alone remained calm in the midst of all the confusion.

senses.definition_vi: trong khi một điều gì đó đang xảy ra hoặc đang được thực hiện; trong khi bạn đang làm gì đó

senses.definition: very small in size or amount; as small as possible

examples.x: The work was carried out at minimal cost.
There's only a minimal amount of risk involved.
The damage to the car was minimal.

senses.definition_vi: rất nhỏ về kích thước hoặc số lượng; nhỏ nhất có thể

senses.definition: not very large, important or serious

examples.x: The new plan involves widening a minor road through the valley.
Both the driver and the passenger suffered minor injuries.
You may need to undergo minor surgery.
Most of these youths are in prison for minor offences.
minor modifications/adjustments
There may be some minor changes to the schedule.
He played a relatively minor role in the organization.
The minor characters in the story are all well drawn.
When you drive a classic car, you expect a few minor problems.

senses.definition_vi: không lớn, không quan trọng hoặc không nghiêm trọng lắm

senses.definition: based on a scale in which the third note is a semitone / half step higher than the second note

examples.x: the key of C minor

senses.definition_vi: dựa trên một thang âm mà nốt thứ ba cao hơn nốt thứ hai một nửa cung

senses.definition: extremely small

examples.x: minute amounts of chemicals in the water
The kitchen on the boat is minute.

senses.definition_vi: mỗi 60 phần của một giờ, bằng 60 giây

senses.definition: very detailed, careful and complete

examples.x: a minute examination/inspection
She remembered everything in minute detail/in the minutest detail(s).

senses.definition_vi: mỗi 60 phần của một giờ, bằng 60 giây

senses.definition: giving the wrong idea or impression and making you believe something that is not true

examples.x: misleading information/advertisements
It would be seriously misleading to suggest that television has no effect on children.

senses.definition_vi: đưa ra ý tưởng hoặc ấn tượng sai lầm và khiến bạn tin vào điều không đúng sự thật

senses.definition: to be or arrive too late for something

examples.x: If I don't leave now I'll miss my plane.
Sorry I'm late—have I missed anything?
‘Is Ann there?’ ‘You've just missed her (= she has just left).’
You'd better hurry—you don't want to miss the bus.
If you miss the deadline, you'll have to pay a fine.

senses.definition_vi: bị hoặc đến muộn một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to fail to be or go somewhere

examples.x: She hasn't missed a game all year.
You missed a good party last night (= because you did not go).
‘Are you coming to the school play?’ ‘I wouldn't miss it for the world.’

senses.definition_vi: không đến hoặc không đi đâu đó

senses.definition: to fail to do something

examples.x: You can't afford to miss meals (= not eat meals) when you're in training.
You have to miss a turn (= to not play when it is your turn in a game).

senses.definition_vi: không làm được điều gì đó

senses.definition: to not take the opportunity to do something

examples.x: The sale prices were too good to miss.
It was an opportunity not to be missed.
She missed the opportunity to take part.
Jackson never missed a chance to serve as teacher and mentor.
The film is a real missed opportunity—it could have been so much better.

senses.definition_vi: không tận dụng cơ hội để làm điều gì đó

senses.definition: to fail to hit, catch, reach, etc. something

examples.x: How many goals has he missed this season?
The bullet missed her by about six inches.
It was a joke that missed its target.
The company has missed all its targets this year.
The van slid on the ice and narrowly missed colliding with us.
She narrowly missed hitting him.

senses.definition_vi: không đánh trúng, bắt được, chạm tới, v.v. một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to fail to hear, see or notice something

examples.x: The hotel is the only white building on the road—you can't miss it.
Don't miss next week's issue!
I missed her name.
No one will want to miss this film.
Your mother will know who's moved in—she doesn't miss much.
When you painted your bedroom, you missed a bit (= of the wall) under the window.

senses.definition_vi: không nghe, nhìn hoặc nhận thấy điều gì đó

senses.definition: to fail to understand something

examples.x: He completely missed the joke.
You're missing the point (= failing to understand the main part) of what I'm saying.
I think I must have missed something because none of this makes any sense.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu điều gì đó

senses.definition: to feel sad because you can no longer see somebody or do something that you like

examples.x: I still miss her a lot.
Your father misses you dreadfully.
She will be greatly missed when she leaves.
Anne, who died on 22 July, will be sadly missed by all who knew her.
What did you miss most when you were in France?
I'm really going to miss your cooking.
I don't miss getting up at six every morning!

senses.definition_vi: cảm thấy buồn vì bạn không còn nhìn thấy ai đó hoặc làm điều gì đó bạn thích nữa

senses.definition: to notice that somebody/something is not where they/it should be

examples.x: When did you first miss the necklace?
Let’s go for a quick drink—nobody will miss us.
We seem to be missing some students this morning.

senses.definition_vi: nhận thấy ai đó/cái gì đó không ở nơi họ/nó nên ở

senses.definition: to avoid something unpleasant

examples.x: If you go now you should miss the crowds.
He fell and just missed knocking the whole display over.

senses.definition_vi: tránh một điều gì đó khó chịu

senses.definition: to not work correctly because the petrol does not burn at the right time
senses.definition_vi: không hoạt động đúng cách vì xăng không cháy đúng lúc

senses.definition: used to say that somebody has a sudden feeling of fear, excitement, etc.

examples.x: My heart missed a beat when I saw who it was.

senses.definition_vi: dùng để nói rằng ai đó có cảm giác sợ hãi, phấn khích, v.v. đột ngột

senses.definition: used to say that somebody notices every opportunity to gain an advantage
senses.definition_vi: dùng để nói rằng ai đó nhận thấy mọi cơ hội để giành lợi thế

senses.definition: to succeed/fail in achieving or guessing something

examples.x: He blushed furiously and Robyn knew she had hit the mark.
The film misses the mark because it just isn't believable.

senses.definition_vi: thành công/thất bại trong việc đạt được hoặc đoán một cái gì đó

senses.definition: to be unable to take advantage of something because you are too late

examples.x: If you don't buy now, you may find that you've missed the boat.

senses.definition_vi: không thể tận dụng điều gì đó vì bạn đã quá muộn

senses.definition: to make a mistake

examples.x: Unless I miss my guess, your computer needs a new hard drive.
If you miss your guess, you lose 10 points.

senses.definition_vi: mắc lỗi

senses.definition: that cannot be found or that is not in its usual place; that has been removed, lost or destroyed

examples.x: I never found the missing piece.
Cases with missing data are excluded from the report.
My gloves have been missing for ages.
Two files have gone missing.
Our cat's gone missing again.
The book has two pages missing.
The book has two missing pages.
He didn't notice there was anything missing from his room until later on.

senses.definition_vi: không thể tìm thấy hoặc không ở đúng vị trí của nó; đã bị loại bỏ, bị mất hoặc bị phá hủy

senses.definition: not at home; not found

examples.x: a missing four-year-old girl
They still hoped to find their missing son.
a woman who went missing three months ago
Posters of missing persons lined the walls.

senses.definition_vi: không có ở nhà; không tìm thấy

senses.definition: not present after an accident, battle, etc. but not known to have been killed

examples.x: He was reported missing, presumed dead.
Many soldiers were listed as missing in action.
It was six hours before the seamen were discovered missing.

senses.definition_vi: không có mặt sau một tai nạn, trận chiến, v.v. nhưng không biết là đã chết

senses.definition: not included, often when it should have been

examples.x: Fill in the missing words in this text.
There were several candidates missing from the list.
What is missing from the production is any sense of emotional commitment.

senses.definition_vi: không được bao gồm, thường là khi lẽ ra phải có

senses.definition: an action or an opinion that is not correct, or that produces a result that you did not want

examples.x: It's easy to make a mistake.
Don't worry, we all make mistakes.
You are making a big mistake.
Leaving school so young was the biggest mistake of my life.
a terrible/serious/huge mistake
It’s a common mistake (= one that a lot of people make).
You must try to learn from your mistakes.
He is determined not to repeat the mistakes of his predecessors.
This letter is addressed to someone else—there must be some mistake.
I made the mistake of giving him my address.

examples.cf: it is a mistake to do something
examples.x: It would be a mistake to ignore his opinion.
It was a big mistake on my part to have trusted her.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: a word, figure, etc. that is not said or written down correctly

examples.x: It's a common mistake among learners of English.
Her essay is full of spelling mistakes.
If students correct their own mistakes, learning improves.
The waiter made a mistake (in) adding up the bill.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to show that you are sure about the truth of what you have just said

examples.x: This is a strange business and no mistake.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: by accident; without intending to

examples.x: I took your bag instead of mine by mistake.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: thinking that something is something else

examples.x: Children may eat pills in mistake for sweets.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: used to emphasize what you are saying, especially when you want to warn somebody about something

examples.x: Make no mistake (about it), this is one crisis that won’t just go away.

senses.definition_vi: không hiểu hoặc đánh giá đúng ai đó/điều gì đó

senses.definition: consisting of different qualities or elements

examples.x: a mixed diet
beaches with mixed sand and shingle

senses.definition_vi: bao gồm các phẩm chất hoặc yếu tố khác nhau

senses.definition: having both good and bad qualities or feelings

examples.x: I still have mixed feelings about going to Brazil (= I am not sure what to think).
I listened to her story with mixed emotions.
These studies have produced mixed results.
The results were decidedly mixed.
The weather has been very mixed recently.
Having a famous father can be a mixed blessing.
The play was given a mixed reception by the critics (= some liked it, some did not).
The film met with a mixed reaction from viewers and critics.
British athletes had mixed fortunes in yesterday's competition.

senses.definition_vi: có cả phẩm chất hoặc cảm xúc tốt và xấu

senses.definition: consisting of different kinds of people, for example, people from different races and cultures

examples.x: an ethnically mixed community
people of mixed race
a mixed marriage (= between two people of different races or religions)

senses.definition_vi: bao gồm các loại người khác nhau, ví dụ, người từ các chủng tộc và nền văn hóa khác nhau

senses.definition: consisting of different types of the same thing

examples.x: a mixed salad
I served chicken with mixed vegetables.
a mixed woodland of ash, oak and birch
The students in the class are of mixed ability (= different levels of ability).

senses.definition_vi: bao gồm các loại khác nhau của cùng một thứ

senses.definition: for or including members of both sexes

examples.x: a mixed school
I'd rather not talk about it in mixed company.

senses.definition_vi: dành cho hoặc bao gồm các thành viên của cả hai giới

senses.definition: that is neither very good, large, hot, etc. nor very bad, small, cold, etc.

examples.x: students of moderate ability
Even moderate amounts of the drug can be fatal.
The team enjoyed only moderate success last season.
Cook over a moderate heat.

senses.definition_vi: không quá tốt, lớn, nóng, v.v. cũng không quá tệ, nhỏ, lạnh, v.v.

senses.definition: having or showing opinions, especially about politics, that are not extreme

examples.x: moderate views/policies
a moderate socialist

senses.definition_vi: có hoặc thể hiện các ý kiến, đặc biệt là về chính trị, không cực đoan

senses.definition: staying within limits that are considered to be reasonable by most people

examples.x: a moderate drinker
moderate wage demands

senses.definition_vi: nằm trong giới hạn được hầu hết mọi người coi là hợp lý

senses.definition: a very short period of time

examples.x: Could you wait a moment, please?
One moment, please (= Please wait a short time).
He thought for a moment before replying.
For one brief moment I thought, ‘I can handle this.’
I'll be back in a moment.
Have you got a moment?
This won't take a moment.
We arrived not a moment too soon (= almost too late).
Moments later (= a very short time later), I heard a terrible crash.

senses.definition_vi: một khoảng thời gian rất ngắn

senses.definition: an exact point in time

examples.x: We're busy at the moment (= now).
At that very moment, the phone rang.
You need to be aware of what you are doing at any given moment.
I agreed in a moment of weakness.
From that moment on, she never felt really well again.

senses.definition_vi: một điểm thời gian chính xác

senses.definition: a good time for doing something; an opportunity

examples.x: I'm waiting for the right moment to tell him the bad news.
Have I caught you at a bad moment?

senses.definition_vi: một thời điểm tốt để làm điều gì đó; một cơ hội

senses.definition: a particular time in somebody's life, or in the course of an event or the development of something

examples.x: That was one of the happiest moments of my life.
Her finest moment came when she won Wimbledon.
The film has many memorable moments.
a great moment in the country's history
This referendum is a defining moment for our nation.
I managed to capture the moment on film.
Enjoy your moment of fame!

senses.definition_vi: một thời điểm cụ thể trong cuộc đời ai đó, hoặc trong diễn biến của một sự kiện hoặc sự phát triển của một cái gì đó

senses.definition: very soon

examples.x: Hurry up! He'll be back any moment now.
He might wake up at any moment.

senses.definition_vi: rất sớm

senses.definition: not long in advance; without warning or time for preparation

examples.x: This was the best room we could get at such short notice.
You must be ready to leave at a moment's notice.

senses.definition_vi: không lâu trước đó; không có cảnh báo hoặc thời gian để chuẩn bị

senses.definition: now, at the present time

examples.x: At this moment in time, I don't know what my decision will be.

senses.definition_vi: bây giờ, tại thời điểm hiện tại

senses.definition: to be popular for a short time (used about something that is not usually popular)

examples.x: The previously unfashionable Tyrol is currently having a moment.
Classic '70s hairstyles are having a moment once more.

senses.definition_vi: phổ biến trong một thời gian ngắn (được sử dụng cho một cái gì đó không thường phổ biến)

senses.definition: to not act normally for a short time, for example when you forget where you are or what you are doing

examples.x: Sorry, I was just having a moment. What time is it?

senses.definition_vi: không hành động bình thường trong một thời gian ngắn, ví dụ khi bạn quên mình đang ở đâu hoặc đang làm gì

senses.definition: to have a short argument or romantic exchange

examples.x: Oh, sorry—were you two having a moment?

senses.definition_vi: có một cuộc tranh cãi ngắn hoặc trao đổi lãng mạn

senses.definition: for now; for a short time

examples.x: This house is big enough for the moment, but we'll have to move if we have children.

senses.definition_vi: hiện tại; trong một thời gian ngắn

senses.definition: to have short times that are better, more interesting, etc. than others

examples.x: The job isn't exciting all the time, but it has its moments.
I found the play rather boring, but it had its moments.

senses.definition_vi: có những khoảng thời gian ngắn tốt hơn, thú vị hơn, v.v. so với những khoảng thời gian khác

senses.definition: completely mentally involved in what you are doing or experiencing

examples.x: The time goes so quickly—you just have to remember to stay in the moment.

senses.definition_vi: hoàn toàn tham gia về mặt tinh thần vào những gì bạn đang làm hoặc trải nghiệm

senses.definition: used to ask somebody to wait for a short time

examples.x: ‘Is Mr Burns available?’ ‘Just a second, please—I'll check.’

senses.definition_vi: để yêu cầu ai đó đợi trong một thời gian ngắn

senses.definition: the latest possible time before an important event

examples.x: They changed the plans at the last minute.
Don't leave your decision to the last moment.

senses.definition_vi: thời điểm cuối cùng có thể trước một sự kiện quan trọng

senses.definition: as soon as…

examples.x: I want to see him the moment he arrives.
The moment she walked through the door I thought she looked different.
I felt at home here from the very moment I arrived.

senses.definition_vi: ngay khi...

senses.definition: a time when somebody/something is tested, or when important decisions are made

examples.x: The moment of truth is when the trainee pilots take over the controls of the plane.

senses.definition_vi: một thời điểm khi ai đó/cái gì đó được thử thách, hoặc khi các quyết định quan trọng được đưa ra

senses.definition: certainly not; not at all

examples.x: I don't think for a moment that she'll accept but you can ask her.

senses.definition_vi: chắc chắn không; hoàn toàn không

senses.definition: very important

examples.x: matters of great moment

senses.definition_vi: rất quan trọng

senses.definition: famous, important and talked about a lot now

examples.x: She's the fashion designer of the moment.

senses.definition_vi: nổi tiếng, quan trọng và được nói đến nhiều hiện nay

senses.definition: suddenly, without planning in advance

examples.x: I phoned him up on the spur of the moment.
a spur-of-the-moment decision

senses.definition_vi: đột ngột, không lên kế hoạch trước

senses.definition: the best time to do something in order for it to be successful

examples.x: The trick is in finding the (right) psychological moment to ask him for more money.
